messages:
maria: heads-up — us-east-1 dedicated GPU pool just hit 100% alloc (all p4d/rtx combos). we're seeing queued requests on the autoscaler and some customers are getting 503s.

jason: confirmed from metrics — 5 min sustained queue, fallback policy kicked for a few tenants. logs show 'POOL_EXHAUSTION' from scheduler.

priya: tagging impacted customers now. do we have a safe traffic-shift plan to move non-critical workloads to hosted in another region?

alan: we configured automatic spillover to hosted for burst earlier, but routing is rate-limited. I'm seeing rate-limiter at ~70% throttle to hosted-us-east-1 and cross-region latency concerns for eu customers.

maria: ok action list: 1) widen hosted spillover limits for low-prio tenants, 2) temporarily drain non-SLA instances from dedicated pool if needed, 3) start proactive rebalancing to us-west-2. who can run the drift?

jason: I can take rebalancing. I'll run the placement move for batch jobs and non-prod.

priya: I'll handle comms and escalate to account success for any enterprise customers. drafting message now. :loudspeaker:

alan: ops-runner, can you bump the hosted spillover caps for the next 30 minutes? need to double the concurrency for low-prio routing.

ops-runner: sure. running update:```json
{"route":"dedicated->hosted","priority":"low","concurrency_limit":200,"duration":"30m"}```

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — 1742101234: Dedicated pool capacity exhaustion in us-east-1. Spillover to hosted enabled. Affected: 12 tenants (6 low-prio). ETA for partial relief: 12-20 minutes.

maria: jason, when you start moves please use the --preserve-cache flag to avoid KV reloads. also watch model-variant compatibility (quantized vs fp16).

jason: starting rebalancer now. command: `redwoodctl rebalance --from=dedicated-us-east-1 --to=dedicated-us-west-2 --filter=nonprod,low-prio --preserve-cache`

alan: note: networking team just flagged a transient packet loss to our transit peer in us-east — that may be part of the degradation. raising ticket with netops (NETOPS-449).

priya: posted comms to affected customer channels. included mitigation steps and ETA.

ops-runner: hosted throttle lift applied. monitoring ingress -> hosted latency and error rate.

sre-bot: METRICS: queue depth reduced 40% in 6 minutes, hosted errors up 1.2% (expected), p50 latency for cross-region requests increased ~70ms.

maria: good. once rebalancer finishes, we'll evaluate whether to scale up the dedicated autoscaler. cost/commit note — scaling dedicated now will impact committed capacity billing; prefer short-term shifts first.

jason: rebalancer finished for first batch. 40 instances moved, cache preserved. no model-mismatch errors.

priya: customers acknowledging and ok with the temporary routing. one enterprise asked for SLA exception log — I attached the sre-bot incident note.

alan: NETOPS updated: packet loss resolved at 1742101480. looks like external peer flap.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (partial) — Dedicated capacity recovered to 85% after moves. Continued monitoring for 2h.

maria: postmortem owners: alan (network), jason (rebalancing), priya (customer comms). please capture timeline, what triggered pool exhaustion (we suspect a batch job spike + peer flap), and improvements: more aggressive preemptible draining, faster hosted ramp, and better cross-region routing fallback.

jason: adding small follow-up: propose a new runbook step to auto-detect batch job spikes and throttle scheduling to dedicated pools.

maria: agreed. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
